Subject: Re: Hosted SSE p99 spike — triage notes

Triage so far (initial):
- Observed elevated tail latency correlated with model variant v2.3-quant serving ~heavy prefixes. KV cache eviction rates spiked ~3x at 20:58 PT.
- Autoscaler observed frequent scale-outs then immediate scale-ins (flapping) for the hosted pool in us-west-2 between 20:50-21:10 PT — suspected noisy neighbour + seq length pattern change.
- Error type analysis: majority are 503s from overloaded inference workers, small fraction (0.2%) are websocket disconnects due to 503s during token stream handshake.

Immediate mitigations I recommend now:
1) Route Chatterly's traffic to model v2.2 (compatible API) as a fast fallback — no schema changes required.
2) Increase instance-min for the relevant pool (hosted) to stabilize autoscaling for the next 60m.
3) Disable aggressive batching heuristics for the pool serving streaming for the next 30m to reduce tail latencies.

I can apply 1+2 in the next 8-12 minutes and post results. If that doesn't materially improve p99 in 20 minutes we'll consider a hotfix rollback for v2.3-quant.

—Dev
